ORAL ORDER 1. Heard learned advocates for the respective parties.
2. By of the present appeal under Section 14-A of the Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, the appellants have prayed to quash and set aside the order dated 01.08.2024 passed in Criminal Case No.753 of 2024 by the learned 4th Additional Sessions Judge, Anand and be further pleased to release the appellants in connection with Application No.821 of 2024 registered at Vidhyanagar, Police Station under Sections 85, 296, 316(2), 318(4) of BNS / Sections 498b, 294b, 406, 420 and 114 of the IPC.
3.

At the outset, it is worth to mention that no complaint has been registered, but the appellants are apprehensive of their arrest in connection with offences alleged in Application No. 821 NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1810/2024 ORDER DATED: 10/01/2025 undefined of 2024, registered at Vidhyanagar Police Station.

sentences.text:
It is submitted that the applicant has preferred an anticipatory bail application, Criminal Misc.
Application No. 753 of 2024, which was rejected by the learned Additional Sessions Judge, Anand,
vide order dated 01.08.2024.
5.

Being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the same, the appellants have preferred this appeal under Section 14-A of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989.
6.

entities.text: Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: During the pendency of the said proceedings, the Police Sub-Inspector, Mr. M.M. Juja of the Vidhyanagar Police Station, has submitted a report, which is taken on record.
The statements recorded by the complainant and her father are also taken on record.
It appears that the parties have approached the authority as husband and wife and have settled the dispute.
The said application has already been filed, and no offence has been registered.
6. In view of the above, as no offence has been registered, the question of granting any pre-arrest bail does not arise in the absence of any apprehension of arrest.
7. Even upon instructions, the learned APP has clearly submitted that, in connection with the same set of facts, the concerned authority will not arrest the appellants.
As the settlement arrived at between the parties and no offence is registered against the appellant, the question of arresting the appellants does not arise.
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1810/2024 ORDER DATED: 10/01/2025 undefined 8.

In view of above, the present appeal stands disposed of with a liberty to file afresh proceedings, if any proceedings be initiated against the appellants based on similar set of allegations leveled in the impugned application/complaint.
This Court has not gone into the merits of the case.
